newsitem.title: CHINA: CITIC Pac upgrade seen neutral for bond.
newsitem.headline: CITIC Pac upgrade seen neutral for bond.

text.p: CITIC Pacific's upcoming Yankee bond is unlikely to benefit much from a ratings upgrade as currency woes continue to slam Hong Kong corporate debt in the U.S. bond market, traders said on Tuesday.
"A one-notch rating upgrade would not help much," a trader at a European investment bank said.
Moody's Investors Service said it had raised the long-term senior debt rating of CITIC Pacific Finance Ltd, guaranteed by CITIC Pacific Ltd, to Baa1 from Baa2.
CITIC Pacific's issue is expected to be US$300 million in size with a tenor of ten years. JP Morgan is tipped to be the lead manager.

A3-rated Hutchison Whampoa's senior unsecured Yankee bond due in 2007 has widened by 10 basis points to 93 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries since Friday when the Hong Kong dollar came under speculative attack, traders said.
The issue was priced at 82 basis points over the benchmark when it was launched at the end of July and had tightened to 75 basis points before the Hong Kong dollar was targetted.
The Hong Kong dollar slipped to a low of HK$7.7430 to the U.S. dollar on Tuesday before firming to close at HK$7.7385/95.
The Hong Kong dollar is the last major currency in Asia to be pegged to the U.S. dollar now that many Asian countries have de-linked their currencies, effectively devaluing them.
